title.en: Define class limits, boundaries, width and mid-value
Convert inclusive classes to exclusive classes

say.en: The marks of 50 students run from 20 to 86. A row for every mark would make a table 67 rows long. Grouping marks into classes like 20-30 makes it short and clear. In this lesson: Define class limits, boundaries, width and mid-value.
Convert inclusive classes to exclusive classes.
Use Sturges' rule.

title.en: Terms of a continuous frequency distribution

body.en: A class interval such as 20–30 has a lower limit (20) and an upper limit (30). Class width h = upper limit − lower limit (for exclusive classes). Mid-value = (lower limit + upper limit)/2. In the exclusive method (10–20, 20–30) the upper limit is not included in the class. In the inclusive method (10–19, 20–29) both limits are included; to get class boundaries, subtract half the gap d/2 from each lower limit and add it to each upper limit. A class with one limit missing ("below 10") is an open-end class.
body.kn: ವರ್ಗಾಂತರ 20–30 ಕ್ಕೆ ಕೆಳ ಮಿತಿ 20, ಮೇಲ್ಮಿತಿ 30. ವರ್ಗದ ಅಗಲ h = ಮೇಲ್ಮಿತಿ − ಕೆಳಮಿತಿ. ಮಧ್ಯಮೌಲ್ಯ = (ಕೆಳಮಿತಿ + ಮೇಲ್ಮಿತಿ)/2. ಬಹಿಷ್ಕೃತ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಮೇಲ್ಮಿತಿ ಸೇರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಅಂತರ್ಗತ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡೂ ಮಿತಿಗಳು ಸೇರುತ್ತವೆ, ವರ್ಗ ಗಡಿಗಳಿಗೆ d/2 ಹೊಂದಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಒಂದು ಮಿತಿ ಇಲ್ಲದ ವರ್ಗ ತೆರೆದ ತುದಿಯ ವರ್ಗ.

Exclusive vs inclusive.

Take the class 20 to 30 on a number line.
Lower limit 20, upper limit 30. Width is 30 minus 20, ten. Mid-value is 25.
Inclusive classes 10–19, 20–29 leave a gap of 1. Subtract and add half the gap.
The boundaries become 9.5–19.5, 19.5–29.5 and 29.5–39.5: no gaps now.

body.en: Usually 5 to 15 *classes* are used. H. A. Sturges suggested $k = 1 + 3.322 \log_{10} N$ classes, and a width of about range ÷ k, rounded to a convenient number. Classes should be of equal width where possible, and must not overlap.
body.kn: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿ 5 ರಿಂದ 15 ವರ್ಗಗಳು. ಸ್ಟರ್ಜಸ್ ನಿಯಮ: k = 1 + 3.322 log N; ಅಗಲ ≈ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ ÷ k. ವರ್ಗಗಳು ಸಮ ಅಗಲದವಾಗಿದ್ದು ಒಂದರೊಳಗೊಂದು ಸೇರಬಾರದು.

problem.en: The marks of 50 students range from 20 to 86. Use Sturges' rule to decide the number of classes and the width, and write the classes.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. The marks of 50 students range from 20 to 86. Use Sturges' rule to decide the number of classes and the width, and write the classes.

say.en: Let us work this out together. The marks of 50 students range from 20 to 86. Use Sturges' rule to decide the number of classes and the width, and write the classes.
k equals 1 plus 3.322 log 50 equals 1 plus 3.322 times 1.6990 equals 6.64 is approximately 7.
Width is approximately 86 minus 20 divided by 6.64 equals 9.93 is approximately 10.
So the answer is 7 classes of width 10, from 20-30 to 80-90.
